know_how.title: Restaurants
know_how.text: Coperto is a per-person cover charge, not a tip. If the bill says “servizio incluso,” don’t add more. Otherwise round up, leave €1 to €2 each, or up to about 10% for great service. Card machines often have no tip option, so carry coins.

know_how.title: Cafés
know_how.text: Pay at the register, then show your receipt at the bar. Standing is cheaper than sitting. Small change on the counter is a nice, optional thank-you.

know_how.title: Taxis
know_how.text: Round up to the next euro, a little more if the driver helps with bags.

know_how.title: Hotels
know_how.text: About €1 to €2 per bag for a porter. €1 to €2 a night for housekeeping is kind, not expected. Firenze adds a nightly tourist tax at the hotel, often not in the booking price.

know_how.title: Guided tours
know_how.text: €5 to €10 per person is a common thank-you for a good group tour.

know_how.title: Restrooms
know_how.text: Public ones often cost a coin. Keep change handy.

know_how.title: Churches
know_how.text: Shoulders and knees covered, for the Duomo, Santa Croce and Santa Maria Novella. It’s enforced at the door. A light scarf in your bag solves it.

know_how.title: Pickpockets
know_how.text: Keep your bag zipped and in front in crowds: Santa Maria Novella station, the Duomo line, the Ponte Vecchio, the San Lorenzo market and busy city buses. Phone in a front pocket, not on the café table.

know_how.title: Street scams
know_how.text: If someone ties a “free” bracelet on your wrist, hands you a rose, or asks you to sign a petition, say “No, grazie” and keep walking. Buy museum tickets only on the official sites, not from people outside.

know_how.title: Getting home at night
know_how.text: Take a taxi home: call one or book it in the itTaxi or appTaxi app (numbers in Taxis), or walk to a rank; the station rank runs 24 hours. Women riding between 21:00 and 4:00 get 10% off (Taxi Rosa); ask when you call. The center is lively and generally comfortable late; Cascine park is best avoided after dark.

know_how.title: Paying
know_how.text: If a card machine offers to charge you in dollars, choose euros. The dollar option usually costs more.

emergency.label: Police, ambulance, fire. English spoken. The old numbers 113, 118 and 115 also still connect to 112.

embassies.label: US Consulate General, Florence (official contact page)

emergency_note: Pharmacies have a green cross sign. One pharmacy in each area stays open at night on a rota; the address is posted on every pharmacy door. To report a theft for insurance, go to a police station (Questura or Carabinieri) with your passport.

voice_help.title: iPhone
voice_help.text: Settings, Accessibility, Spoken Content, Voices, Italian. Pick a voice and download its Enhanced or Premium version.

voice_help.title: Android
voice_help.text: Settings, search for Text-to-speech, preferred engine settings, install voice data, Italian. Menu names vary by phone.

travel_notes: In Firenze, locals drink coffee standing at the bar. A table usually costs more, so do as the locals do.
The row of windows above the Ponte Vecchio shops is the Vasari Corridor, built so the Medici could cross the river unseen.
Pay at the register first, then hand your receipt to the barista.
From the Bardini Garden the dome looks close enough to touch, with a fraction of the crowds at Piazzale Michelangelo.
Shoulders and knees covered for churches. A light scarf in your bag solves it.
